checkModulesEntryFullReportKGraph (DriveArgs inputs valueMain _ preludeKey _ runtimeDecls coreDecls0 modules0) =
  -- The single-file front door loads stdlib/core.mdk twice: once as its prelude and
  -- once as the singleton `__user__` module.  Resolve already owns the syntactic
  -- self-test that prevents double-seeding core.  Apply that same authority before
  -- identity stamping, so one declaration graph is not stamped once as `core` and
  -- again as `__user__`.  `None` also prevents the empty prelude pass from sharing a
  -- memo key with the separately loaded declarations we deliberately dropped.
  -- Partial lookalikes remain ordinary because `programIsCore` requires BOTH halves.
  let (effectivePreludeKey, effectiveCoreDecls0, effectiveModules0) =
    match modules0
      [(_, prog)] =>
        if programIsCore prog then
          (None, [], [("core", prog)])
        else
          (preludeKey, coreDecls0, modules0)
      _ => (preludeKey, coreDecls0, modules0)
  let g =
    driveGraphK
      GOutDiags
      (driveArgs
        inputs
        valueMain
        effectivePreludeKey
        runtimeDecls
        effectiveCoreDecls0
        effectiveModules0)
  ((g.gdReport, g.gdOutputs), g.gdGraph)

-- render the entry report: type errors win (each `TYPE ERROR: …`), else the
-- entry's `name : scheme` lines followed by its non-exhaustive-match warnings.
-- The harness sorts, so scheme/warn relative order is not load-bearing.  Mirrors
-- runCheck's single-file shape, but over the entry module of a resolved graph.
export
checkModulesEntryReport : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  String
checkModulesEntryReport inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules =
  fst (checkModulesEntryReportOut inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules)

-- `checkModulesEntryReport` beside the outputs of its drive.
checkModulesEntryReportOut : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (String, DriveOutputs)
checkModulesEntryReportOut inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules =
  let (report, outputs) =
    checkModulesEntryFullReportK
      inputs
      False
      None
      runtimeDecls
      coreDecls
      modules
  let (_, schemes, errs, warns) = entrySplit report
  match errs
    [] => (joinNl (schemeLines schemes ++ map tcMsg warns), outputs)
    _ => (joinNl (typeErrorLines (map tcMsg errs)), outputs)

-- exit-code predicate analog of checkHasErrors: any type error in ANY module of
-- the resolved graph (entry or imported — see checkModulesEntryFromDiags).
export
checkModulesEntryHasErrors : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  Bool
checkModulesEntryHasErrors inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules =
  let (_, errs, _) = checkModulesEntryFull inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules
  match errs
    [] => False
    _ => True

-- ── ONE-MODULE Module-arm wrapper (S-check-one-wrapper, E-1 #1115) ─────────
-- The scheme/diagnostic-tree analogue of `elaborateOne` (above): runs a SINGLE
-- program through the `Module` arm as a degenerate one-entry module list, the
-- same way `elaborateOne` runs it through `elaborateModules`.  `checkModulesEntryFull`
-- is the entry-report projection of the one whole-graph driver (see the file header
-- and `driveGraphK`) — it therefore performs BOTH halves of the
-- two-part safety property a standalone `Module`-arm caller must uphold
-- (`mintGraphCtx` and the unconditional `mangledFunDefsPresentRef`/
-- `declEnvsRef` overwrites, the last carrying the method and constructor export
-- indices — see `checkModuleFullDiags`'s header comment just above its `export`).
-- Delegating to it (rather than hand-assembling a bare `checkModuleFullDiags` call
-- with an invented module id / degenerate accData/implDecls) gets that property for
-- free and needs no "empty module id" convention of its own — `foldModules`'s own
-- singleton-list clause (`[(mid, prog)]`) already IS the degenerate one-entry case,
-- run through the identical preamble every N-module call gets.  `rootId` names the
-- program's own module id (analogous to `elaborateOne`'s `rootId`); `checkModulesEntryFull`
-- has previously only been reached with 2+-module graphs (`checkModulesEntryReport`/
-- `checkModulesEntryHasErrors`, both import-bearing-only per its own header comment) —
-- this is its first 1-module caller.
export
checkOneScheme : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  List (String, Scheme)
checkOneScheme inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls (rootId, prog) =
  let (schemes, _, _) =
    checkModulesEntryFull inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls [(rootId, prog)]
  pubSchemes schemes

-- FULL-ENVIRONMENT sibling of `checkOneScheme` (S-full-env-scheme-entry, #1116),
-- `checkOneSchemeFullK`:
-- `(preludeSchemes, ownSchemes)` for a ONE-MODULE program, the Module-arm
-- replacement for the retired single-program environment that the
-- introspection consumers (LSP hover/completion/inlayHint, the playground's
-- hover/complete query, `check-policy --fn <name>`) need: they look names up by
-- BARE NAME with no idea whether the name is the user's or the prelude's, so
-- `checkOneScheme`'s terminal-module-own-only answer is not enough for them.
--
-- The two halves are handed back SEPARATE, not pre-concatenated, so the caller
-- states the precedence it wants explicitly.  Every current consumer wants
-- `own ++ prelude` (first match wins ⇒ a user redefinition shadows the prelude's
-- binding of the same name) — see `checkModulesEntryFullSplit`'s 🚨 note.  This
-- is NOT a widening of the `medaka check` front door, whose narrowed
-- own-schemes-only report is deliberate and unchanged.
--
-- The prelude key is for the prelude interface (see
-- `checkCoreMemoized`): pass `Some (desugaredPreludeKey runtimeSrc,
-- desugaredPreludeKey coreSrc)` when `runtimeDecls`/`coreDecls` are exactly what
-- `desugaredPrelude` returned for those sources; `None` otherwise.
export
checkOneSchemeFullK : DriveInputs ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (List (String, PubScheme), List (String, PubScheme))
checkOneSchemeFullK inputs preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls prog =
  fst
    (checkOneSchemeFullKGraph
      (driveArgs inputs False preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls [prog]))

-- `checkOneSchemeFullK` beside the graph record its drive ends in, for a test that
-- observes that record after the drive.
export
checkOneSchemeFullKGraph : DriveArgs ->
  ((List (String, PubScheme), List (String, PubScheme)), GraphCtx)
checkOneSchemeFullKGraph args =
  let (report, gctx) = checkOneReportKGraph args
  let (coreSchemes, schemes, _, _) = entrySplit report
  ((coreSchemes, schemes), gctx)

-- diagnostics-returning sibling of `checkOneScheme`, matching the former wrapper's
-- return shape (`(errs, warns)`) exactly, so a call site can swap targets with no
-- shape change (this slice's own acceptance bar — see the packet).
export
checkOneDiags : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (List TcDiag, List TcDiag)
checkOneDiags inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls prog =
  checkOneDiagsK inputs False None runtimeDecls coreDecls prog

-- `checkOneDiags` beside the graph record its drive ends in, for a test that observes
-- that record after the drive.
export
checkOneDiagsGraph : DriveArgs -> ((List TcDiag, List TcDiag), GraphCtx)
checkOneDiagsGraph args =
  let (report, gctx) = checkOneReportKGraph args
  let (_, _, errs, warns) = entrySplit report
  ((errs, warns), gctx)

-- `checkOneDiags` with the prelude key for the prelude interface — same contract as
-- `checkOneSchemeFullK` — and the caller's value-main candidate (`autoPrintWanted`).
export
checkOneDiagsK : DriveInputs ->
  Bool ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  (List TcDiag, List TcDiag)
checkOneDiagsK inputs valueMain preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls prog =
  let (_, _, errs, warns) =
    entrySplit
      (checkOneReportK inputs valueMain preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls prog)
  (errs, warns)

-- The report-returning sibling of both `checkOneSchemeFullK` and `checkOneDiagsK`:
-- the one-module drive's whole report, which each of them projects.
export
checkOneReportK : DriveInputs ->
  Bool ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, List Decl) ->
  TcReport
checkOneReportK inputs valueMain preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls prog =
  fst
    (checkOneReportKGraph
      (driveArgs inputs valueMain preludeKey runtimeDecls coreDecls [prog]))

-- `checkOneReportK` beside the graph record its drive ends in.
checkOneReportKGraph : DriveArgs -> (TcReport, GraphCtx)
checkOneReportKGraph args =
  let ((report, _), gctx) = checkModulesEntryFullReportKGraph args
  (report, gctx)

-- S-migrate-check-route (E-1 #1115): thin ONE-MODULE String/Bool wrappers, matching
-- `checkToLinesWithRuntime`'s / `checkErrorsWithRuntime`'s (runtimeDecls, coreProg,
-- userProg) shape exactly, so `compiler/tools/check.mdk`'s two rendering/bool call
-- sites can swap targets with no shape change.  Delegate to the EXISTING entry-report/
-- -hasErrors functions above (already byte-identical in render logic to
-- checkToLinesWithRuntime/checkErrorsWithRuntime — `joinNl (schemeLines ++ warns)` on
-- success, `typeErrorLines` on error) over a singleton module list, rather than
-- duplicating that rendering logic here.  `"__user__"` mirrors `elaborateOne`'s own
-- rootId convention for a bare/no-import file (`entry_support.mdk`).
export
checkOneToLinesWithRuntime : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (String, DriveOutputs)
checkOneToLinesWithRuntime inputs runtimeDecls coreProg userProg = checkModulesEntryReportOut
  inputs
  runtimeDecls
  coreProg
  [("__user__", userProg)]

-- `checkOneToLinesWithRuntime` with the prelude key for the prelude interface (see
-- `checkCoreMemoized`): same contract as `checkOneSchemeFullK`.  Same render as
-- `checkModulesEntryReport`, over the keyed driver.
export
checkOneToLinesWithRuntimeK : DriveInputs ->
  Option (Int, Int) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  String
checkOneToLinesWithRuntimeK inputs preludeKey runtimeDecls coreProg userProg =
  let (schemes, errs, warns) = checkModulesEntryFullK
    inputs
    preludeKey
    runtimeDecls
    coreProg
    [("__user__", userProg)]
  match errs
    [] => joinNl (schemeLines schemes ++ map tcMsg warns)
    _ => joinNl (typeErrorLines (map tcMsg errs))

export
checkOneToLines : DriveInputs -> List Decl -> String
checkOneToLines inputs userProg =
  fst (checkOneToLinesWithRuntime inputs [] [] userProg)

export
checkOneErrorsWithRuntime : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  Bool
checkOneErrorsWithRuntime inputs runtimeDecls coreProg userProg = checkModulesEntryHasErrors
  inputs
  runtimeDecls
  coreProg
  [("__user__", userProg)]

-- One-module match-report wrapper: the type-aware
-- non-exhaustive-match report for ONE module, runtime externs seeded and NO
-- prelude, rendered as one `Warning: non-exhaustive match …` line per warning.
--
-- WARNINGS ONLY — type errors are dropped on the floor rather than rendered, which
-- is this report's contract, not an oversight: the caller
-- (`compiler/entries/check_match_main.mdk`) diffs against
-- `dev/diagdump.exe --check-match`, which reports match warnings and nothing else.
-- `checkOneDiags` is the wrapper this delegates to precisely because it hands the
-- two halves back SEPARATE, so the split needs no new projection.
--
-- The empty `coreDecls` is what makes the seed identical to the `Flat` wrapper's
-- hand-built `externSchemes (runtimeExternTyOriginScope []) runtimeDecls`: `graphPreamble`
-- computes `externSchemes (runtimeExternTyOriginScope coreDecls) runtimeDecls`, which
-- collapses to the same expression at `coreDecls = []`.  `"__user__"` mirrors
-- `checkOneToLinesWithRuntime`'s rootId convention just above.
export
checkOneMatchToLines : DriveInputs -> List Decl -> List Decl -> String
checkOneMatchToLines inputs runtimeDecls prog =
  let (_, warns) = checkOneDiags inputs runtimeDecls [] ("__user__", prog)
  joinNl (map tcMsg warns)

-- run the multi-module front-end and render the ENTRY module's own bindings as
-- `name : scheme` per line (the harness sorts) — diffs vs dev/tc_module_probe.
export
checkModulesEntryLines : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  String
checkModulesEntryLines inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules =
  joinNl
    (schemeLines
      (entryOwnSchemes (checkModules inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules)))

-- Emit EVERY module's bindings in one pass, each section preceded by a
-- `## MODULE <mid>` marker line.  A single full-closure run can then cover many
-- modules at once (the batch harness splits on the marker and diffs each
-- section vs its per-module oracle).  Scheme of a module depends only on its
-- dependency-closure (which precedes it in topo order), so a module's section
-- is identical whether checked alone or inside a larger union closure.
export
checkModulesAllLines : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  String
checkModulesAllLines inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules =
  joinNl (allModuleLines (checkModules inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls modules))

allModuleLines : List (String, List (String, PubScheme)) -> List String
allModuleLines [] = []
allModuleLines ((mid, ss) :: rest) =
  "## MODULE " ++ mid :: schemeLines ss ++ allModuleLines rest

-- The multi-module analog of `elaborate`: the composition of `checkModules`
-- (per-module-frame typecheck, dependency-first) and the EMethodAt route-
-- stamping `elaborate` does single-module.  prePasses the prelude + every module
-- (rewriting return-position method occurrences to EMethodAt over the WHOLE
-- program's RP method set), typechecks each module in dependency order (seeded
-- like checkModules), and STAMPS each module's route refs from its now-resolved
-- result types.  Returns the SAME trees (refs filled) so evalModulesWith can route
-- return-position dispatch (`pure`/`andThen` — the Parser monad) by RKey instead
-- of the untyped arg-tag fallback.  RKey-only (dictNames = []): the bootstrap
-- source uses no `=>`-constrained user polymorphism, so no EDictAt / dict params
-- and no pendingDictApps / pendingRecDictApps to resolve.  Return shape: `ElabResult`.
export
elaborateModules : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  ElabResult
-- E4: D3b's ARG-position dict-passing per module runs inside the drive
-- (`dictPassModulesIfEnabled`), on every path (single elaboration mode, #157).
--
-- Impl-body inference runs on every driver, so a standalone-shadow method call
-- INSIDE an impl body (map's `Debug`/`Eq`/`Ord`/`Display (Map k v)` bodies all call
-- standalone `toList m`) RECORDS its RLocal site (recordRLocalSite -> the goal
-- channel) for resolveRLocalSites to stamp.  Without it the impl-body `toList` route
-- stays at its default RNone -> eval arg-tag-dispatches a Map through the
-- no-matching-tag `keepOrAll` fallback to Foldable List's `toList = identity` ->
-- returns the Map unchanged -> `debug`/`display` recurse forever (SIGBUS on
-- `medaka test stdlib/map.mdk`).
--
-- #2705: what distinguishes this projection from the diagnostics one is no longer
-- WHAT is solved — the same driver, the same preamble, the same worker, the same
-- graph-end drain — but that `GOutTrees` sets the promotion-eligible set (so its
-- groups PROMOTE and their call sites are marked as dict applications), publishes
-- the evidence table and dict-passes the marked trees, and that it returns the
-- diagnostics the drive raised as its residual.
elaborateModules inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls0 modulesIn =
  match (elaborateModulesWithSchemes
    inputs
    False
    runtimeDecls
    coreDecls0
    modulesIn)
    (result, _, _) => result

-- `elaborateModules` beside the graph record its drive ends in, for a test that
-- observes that record after the drive.
export
elaborateModulesGraph : DriveArgs -> (ElabResult, GraphCtx)
elaborateModulesGraph args =
  let ((result, _, _), gctx) = elabTreesDrive args
  (result, gctx)

-- `elaborateModules` together with the prelude's schemes and the entry module's own
-- schemes, from the SAME drive: a verb that both reads types and evaluates the
-- elaborated program (`check-policy`) typechecks once.  `valueMain` is the caller's
-- value-main candidate (`autoPrintWanted`).
export
elaborateModulesWithSchemes : DriveInputs ->
  Bool ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (ElabResult, List (String, PubScheme), List (String, PubScheme))
elaborateModulesWithSchemes inputs valueMain runtimeDecls coreDecls0 modulesIn =
  let (result, r, _) =
    elaborateModulesWithReport
      inputs
      valueMain
      None
      runtimeDecls
      coreDecls0
      modulesIn
  let (core, entrySchemes, _, _) = entrySplit r
  (result, core, entrySchemes)

-- `elaborateModulesWithSchemes` returning its drive's whole report and outputs
-- beside the elaboration.  `executes` names the `async` driver of a caller that runs or
-- emits the trees: its checked program then carries the auto-print evidence.
export
elaborateModulesWithReport : DriveInputs ->
  Bool ->
  Option String ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (ElabResult, TcReport, DriveOutputs)
elaborateModulesWithReport inputs valueMain executes runtimeDecls coreDecls0 modulesIn =
  fst
    (elabTreesDrive
      (DriveArgs
        inputs
        valueMain
        executes
        None
        None
        runtimeDecls
        coreDecls0
        modulesIn))

-- `elaborateModulesWithReport` keyed as `checkModulesChainReportFor` is: under the
-- prelude generation pair and [chainKey], with one source key per module in
-- [stepKeys], each module before the entry that is unchanged since it was recorded
-- is served from its recorded trees, and each module the drive checks records them.
export
elaborateModulesChainReport : DriveInputs ->
  Bool ->
  (Int, Int) ->
  String ->
  List (Option String) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  (ElabResult, TcReport, DriveOutputs)
elaborateModulesChainReport inputs valueMain (rk, ck) chainKey stepKeys runtimeDecls coreDecls0 modulesIn =
  fst
    (elabTreesDrive
      (DriveArgs
        inputs
        valueMain
        None
        None
        (Some (chainFullKey rk ck chainKey, stepKeys))
        runtimeDecls
        coreDecls0
        modulesIn))

-- The tree-producing drive of [args], as `elaborateModules` projects it.
elabTreesDrive : DriveArgs -> ((ElabResult, TcReport, DriveOutputs), GraphCtx)
elabTreesDrive args = elabDriveResult (driveGraphK GOutTrees args)

elabDriveResult : GraphDrive -> ((ElabResult, TcReport, DriveOutputs), GraphCtx)
elabDriveResult g = (
  (
    (
      g.gdCore,
      g.gdModules,
      map dropModSchemes g.gdPerMod,
      g.gdResidual,
      g.gdEvTable,
      g.gdDispositions,
      ElabFacts {
        efManifests = g.gdOutputs.doManifests,
        efBinders = g.gdBinders,
        efEntryOutcome = g.gdOutputs.doEntryOutcome,
      },
    ),
    g.gdReport,
    g.gdOutputs,
  ),
  g.gdGraph,
)

-- The report of `elaborateModules`' drive, for a test that reads it.
export
elaborateModulesReport : DriveInputs ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List Decl) ->
  TcReport
elaborateModulesReport inputs runtimeDecls coreDecls0 modulesIn =
  match (elaborateModulesWithReport
    inputs
    False
    None
    runtimeDecls
    coreDecls0
    modulesIn)
    (_, report, _) => report
-- arg-position interface-method names whose route resolveArgStamps may stamp
-- (populated on every path; an empty set would degenerate prePassDictArg to prePassDict)

-- DRIVER-COLLAPSE Phase 2 (global): seed the promotion-eligible set with the USER
-- modules' top-level fn names (NOT core/prelude — those keep arg-tag / RKey
-- dispatch, which type-checks the goldens).  Seeded on every path (single
-- elaboration mode) so
-- elaborateModules promotes INFERRED-constraint user fns exactly as flat
-- the retired promotion fixpoint did (it reran discovery whenever the eligible set was
-- non-empty).  The TYPECHECK golden module drivers
-- (checkModulesEntryLines/checkModulesDiagsChain) never reach elaborateModules, so their
-- goldens are unaffected; the eval goldens are captured from the OCaml oracle's
-- run, which dict-passes prelude+modules unconditionally — so promotion-on-eval
-- matches them. Mirrors the graph driver's dictionary-eligibility seed.

-- Cause A / Phase 2: promotion discovery — an unsignatured fn whose body dispatches
-- a method in ARG position (`f s = println s` → inferred `Display a => …`) OR uses a
-- return-position method (`doubleEmpty x = append (append x empty) empty` → inferred
-- `Monoid a => …`) is discovered + registered in promotedRef/funConstraintsRef/
-- activeDictVars, and the promoted names join the dict-name set so their call sites
-- are marked EDictAt (caller supplies the dict ARGUMENT) and their defs get the
-- leading dict PARAM.  The discovery is `registerInferredConstraints` at each
-- group's close, and the schedule marks with its result (`markRecursiveOccurrences`
-- for the group's own occurrences, `beginModuleMarking` for every later group and
-- module); the joint-flattened Flat-arm scratch pass survives only in
-- the retired single-program promotion discovery.

-- E6: dict-name set for the `=>`-constrained-function layer, mirroring the
-- single-file emit driver's assembly (llvm_emit_typed_main.runEmit): prelude
-- return- AND arg-position `=>`-constrained fns (clamp/debugListItems/…) plus the
-- modules' own constrained signatures.  Computed on every path (single elaboration
-- mode).
-- Used to MARK constrained-fn call sites EDictAt in the prePass (so the caller
-- supplies the dict ARGUMENT) AND to add the leading dict PARAM in the final
-- dictPass (so the callee body's witness binds).  BOTH halves are required: marking
-- alone under-defines the param; param alone under-applies the call (ABI mismatch).
-- Cause A: promoted (inferred-constraint) user fns join the set.

-- ARGSTAMP-UNIFY Phase 4: the eval-dict layer is now PERMANENTLY active on both
-- paths (flag retired). The former elaborator ran its resolve chain and dict pass
-- UNCONDITIONALLY; the 1-module / multi-module eval path matches, so method-level
-- constraints (`build : Num e =>`) and parametric-impl `requires` (`impl Default
-- (List a) requires Default a`) — which leave dictNames EMPTY (no top-level
-- constrained FUNCTION) but still need resolveMethodDicts / the DImpl dict-pass —
-- get serviced.  The dictPass/resolve passes are no-ops when nothing was marked, so
-- this leaves the golden eval trees byte-identical where there is nothing to
-- dict-pass.
-- C5: ALSO mark cross-module standalone-shadow method occurrences (box's
-- `toList`/`isEmpty`) as EMethodAt, so they carry a route ref for elabModuleStamp's
-- resolveRLocalSites to stamp RLocal.  Without this they stay EVar (arg-position)
-- → no route ref → arg-tag panic on a no-impl
-- receiver.  Only added to the MARK set (not rpNames proper, which discoverPromoted
-- etc. consume) so other passes are unchanged.
-- DRIVER-COLLAPSE Phase 2: ALSO include methodConstraintNames (methods with their OWN
-- method-level `=>` constraint, e.g. `build : Num e => e -> t`), mirroring flat
-- the former pre-pass mark set (`returnPosMethodNames prog ++ methodConstraintNames
-- prog`).  Without it the method-constraint occurrence stays unmarked → its impl
-- clause's leading method-dict param is dropped/mis-bound → `non-exhaustive match`
-- (method_constraint_impl_offset).

-- impl table accumulates across modules (dependency order): a module's
-- arg-position dispatch can thread an EARLIER module's / core's parametric
-- `requires` element dict.  core2 seeds it.

-- E5: dict-pass each module's now-stamped
-- trees, preserving the former final `dictPass`. A parametric `requires`
-- impl whose body element-dispatch E5 routed RDict needs its leading
-- `$dict_<m>_<slot>` PARAM (dictPassDecl's DImpl arm) so the emitter can bind the
-- witness the route references; the call site's impl-dict route (filled by
-- resolveArgStamp) supplies the matching ARGUMENT.  E6: dictNames now carries the
-- prelude/module `=>`-constrained fns (clamp/debugListItems/displayListItems/…),
-- so dictPassDecl's DFunDef arm ALSO prepends their `$dict_<fn>_<slot>` params —
-- closing the "unbound dict witness" residual.  Runs on every path (single
-- elaboration mode); when nothing is marked the pass is a no-op returning
-- core2/modules2 verbatim.

-- Post-ARGSTAMP-UNIFY (Phase 4): ALWAYS run on every path (single elaboration mode).
-- Emit:
-- the DImpl arm prepends parametric impl-body element-dict params even when no
-- top-level `=>`-constrained FUNCTION is in [dictNames] (e.g. the empty-prelude
-- nested_dict_dispatch fixture: a parametric `Cmp (Box a) requires Cmp a` with no
-- constrained fn).  Eval: same — a parametric-impl `requires` whose DImpl body needs
-- its leading element-dict param (nested_instance_dicts: `impl Default (List a)
-- requires Default a`) gets dict-passed even with no top-level constrained FUNCTION.
-- Runs the unconditional final dict pass. No-op when nothing was
-- marked → byte-identical golden trees.  scopePredicateSlots sizes each define's leading
-- dict params to its surviving-constraint count.

-- ── the other half of `selfDeclArities`, and it is NOT optional ──────────────
-- `selfDeclArities` is a per-module VIEW; the ref it is written to is ALSO the ref the
-- cross-module accumulator is snapshotted FROM at the end of the same body
-- (`crossModuleFunConstraintsRef` ← `ModuleCtx.funConstraintsRef`).  Without this restore the
-- view becomes a graph-wide LOSS: the rows masked while checking module `mid` never reach
-- the modules processed after it.
--
-- 🚨 MEASURED, not hypothetical — this is what the first cut of #1425's fix did.  Masking
-- `count` while checking `vector` (which declares an unconstrained `count`) deleted the
-- PRELUDE's constrained `count` row from the accumulator, so every later module lost it and
-- an ordinary `count (x => x > 1) [1, 2, 3]` in the entry panicked at `run`.  Prelude names
-- are the ones that expose it, because `importDefinersOf` skips `core` — a prelude name is
-- never an "explicit import", so it can only ever be answered by this bare table.
--
-- Restores by NAME from the accumulator's own previous value (still unwritten at the
-- snapshot, which is this ref's only writer), appended AFTER the module's rows so
-- first-match still prefers the identity-resolved answer.  Content-preserving: the view
-- removed exactly these rows, so appending them back is not duplication.
selfNameRows : List Decl -> List (String, a) -> List (String, a)
selfNameRows prog old =
  let own = namesToSet (declTopFnNames prog) omEmpty
  filterList (e => omHasKey (fst e) own) old

-- attribute each fn DEFINED in [prog] that carries a per-fn table entry to [mid] —
-- the source-exact `(mid, name)` key every cross-module fn table is read under.
--
-- Used for all three of the fn-side qual snapshots: the constraint ARITIES
-- (`funConstraintsRef`), the slot-parallel IFACES (`funConstraintIfacesRef`) and, since
-- B-2.2-f (#1113), the per-entry DECLARED-PREFIX scalar.  It was two byte-identical
-- monomorphic copies (`attributeModuleArities` / `attributeModuleArrIfaces`), each
-- carrying a `rule-duplicate-body` disable deferred to #1201; the sidecar's SCALAR
-- payload does not fit a `List X` signature at all, so the payload is now `a` and both
-- disables are gone rather than joined by a third.
attributeModuleEntries : String ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, a) ->
  List ((String, String), a)
attributeModuleEntries mid prog entries =
  let progNames = namesToSet (declTopFnNames prog) omEmpty
  map
    (e => ((mid, fst e), snd e))
    (filterList (e => omHasKey (fst e) progNames) entries)

-- #1114 (#845): attribute each TOP-LEVEL binding of [prog] that carries a
-- `schemeObligationsRef` entry to [mid], source-exactly keyed `(mid, name)` — the same
-- key discipline as `attributeModuleEntries` above, and for the same #739 reason (a
-- bare-name cross-module table misattributes a same-named export of another module).
--
-- ⚠️ Unlike the arity tables, `schemeObligationsRef` is keyed `(name, binding-id)` and
-- holds LOCAL/`where` binders too (registerSchemeObligations is called from the local
-- sites with `omEmpty` member ids, so those key under id 0).  Two filters make the
-- projection to a bare exported name safe:
--   (1) [progNames] keeps only names this module defines at TOP LEVEL, so a `where`
--       helper whose name matches nothing at top level never enters the table at all;
--   (2) FIRST-occurrence-wins within a name, which resolves the one residual case — a
--       `where` helper that happens to SHARE a top-level name.  `schemeObligationsRef`
--       is consed, and a group's top-level members are registered AFTER the locals
--       inferred inside their bodies, so the head-most entry for a name is the
--       top-level one.  That is byte-identically the policy the SAME-module use site
--       already applies (`lookupSchemeOblsByName`'s first match), which is the point:
--       an importer must see what a same-module caller sees.
--
-- 🚨 A MODULE'S CONTRIBUTION IS WHAT IT DECLARES *PLUS WHAT IT RE-EXPORTS*, and the second
-- half is not optional — it is the recurrence `.claude/workstreams/TYPECHECK.md` records for
-- #1283 and `renameAliasedMethods` (below) already learned for the METHOD tables: "the
-- decl's origin names the DECLARING module and the import path names the RE-EXPORTER, so
-- the identity test misses."  Attributing only `declTopFnNames prog` means a pure
-- re-exporter (`export import lib.def.{f}`, whose `prog` has no function definitions at
-- all) contributes NOTHING, so `import lib.reexp.{f}` found no entry and #845's whole
-- failure came back one hop out — `check` 0, `build` 0, and the built binary SEGFAULTED.
-- Adversarial review produced exactly that program; this arm is the answer to it.
--
-- [qual] is the ALREADY-ACCUMULATED cross-module table, and dependency-first module order
-- is what makes reading it correct here: every module this one re-exports FROM has been
-- processed already, so its entries are present. That also makes a multi-hop chain resolve
-- without special-casing — each hop re-attributes under its own mid as it is processed,
-- exactly as `reexportedMethodNames` folds the method sets.
--
-- Re-export entries come SECOND so the module's own top-level binding wins the first-match
-- dedup below if a module somehow both defines and re-exports one name.
attributeModuleSchemeObls : String ->
  List Decl ->
  List ((String, String), List VecObl) ->
  List ((String, Int), List VecObl) ->
  List ((String, String), List VecObl)
attributeModuleSchemeObls mid prog qual entries =
  attributeSchemeOblsGo
      mid
      (namesToSet (publicValNames prog) omEmpty)
      omEmpty
      entries
    ++ map (e => ((mid, fst e), snd e)) (reexportSchemeOblEntries prog qual)

-- ⚠️ The export test is `publicValNames`, the module's own canonical one — NOT a
-- hand-rolled `DFunDef True` scan.  A first cut used the latter and REGRESSED two of this
-- PR's own fixtures: `export g : Num a => a -> a` on one line with `g x = x + 1` on the
-- next parses as a PUBLIC `DTypeSig` plus a PRIVATE `DFunDef`, so a scan that only reads
-- the `DFunDef` flag calls an exported binding private and drops it from the store.
-- `publicValNames` already answers this (its `DTypeSig True` arm), and reusing it is what
-- keeps this table's notion of "exported" from drifting from the module seed's.

-- the scheme contexts a module RE-EXPORTS (`export import src.{…}` / `export import src.*`),
-- each under the name it re-exports it as.  Reuses `schemeOblEntriesFor` — the same
-- spelling table the IMPORT side uses — so re-export and import can never disagree about
-- what a spelling binds; that is one table, not two kept in step by hand.
-- ⚠️ `export import src as A` contributes entries keyed `A.<name>`, which no importer of
-- THIS module can name (an alias is local to the file that writes it).  They are inert
-- rather than wrong, and excluding them would mean a second spelling table.
reexportSchemeOblEntries : List Decl ->
  List ((String, String), List VecObl) ->
  List (String, List VecObl)
reexportSchemeOblEntries [] _ = []
reexportSchemeOblEntries ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) qual =
  reexportSchemeOblEntries [d] qual ++ reexportSchemeOblEntries rest qual
reexportSchemeOblEntries ((DUse True path _) :: rest) qual =
  schemeOblEntriesFor (useModId path) path qual
    ++ reexportSchemeOblEntries rest qual
reexportSchemeOblEntries (_ :: rest) qual = reexportSchemeOblEntries rest qual

attributeSchemeOblsGo : String ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  OrdMap Unit ->
  List ((String, Int), List VecObl) ->
  List ((String, String), List VecObl)
attributeSchemeOblsGo _ _ _ [] = []
attributeSchemeOblsGo mid progNames seen (e :: rest)
  | not (omHasKey (fst (fst e)) progNames) =
    attributeSchemeOblsGo mid progNames seen rest
  | omHasKey (fst (fst e)) seen = attributeSchemeOblsGo mid progNames seen rest
  | otherwise =
    ((mid, fst (fst e)), snd e)
      :: attributeSchemeOblsGo
        mid
        progNames
        (omInsert (fst (fst e)) () seen)
        rest

-- WS-2/D2 method analog: attribute each method whose INTERFACE is declared in [prog]
-- (carrying a methodPredicateSlotsRef entry) to [mid].  Keyed by the interface's module —
-- the arity is a property of the method signature, registered during that module's
-- method-row construction pass.  The per-run table also holds the rows imported
-- modules contributed; only keys of [prog]'s own interfaces are attributed here.
attributeMethodModulePredicateSlots : String ->
  List Decl ->
  List (String, List MethodPredicateSlot) ->
  List ((String, String), List MethodPredicateSlot)
attributeMethodModulePredicateSlots mid prog entries =
  let progMethods = namesToSet (ifaceMethodSlotKeys prog) omEmpty
  map
    (e => ((mid, fst e), snd e))
    (filterList (e => omHasKey (fst e) progMethods) entries)

-- The `methodSlotKey` of every method of every interface [prog] declares.
ifaceMethodSlotKeys : List Decl -> List String
ifaceMethodSlotKeys [] = []
ifaceMethodSlotKeys ((DAttrib _ d) :: rest) =
  ifaceMethodSlotKeys [d] ++ ifaceMethodSlotKeys rest
ifaceMethodSlotKeys ((DInterface { name, methods, ifaceOrigin, ... }) :: rest) =
  map
      (methodSlotKey IfaceRef { irName = name, irOrigin = ifaceOrigin })
      (ifaceMethodNames methods)
    ++ ifaceMethodSlotKeys rest
ifaceMethodSlotKeys (_ :: rest) = ifaceMethodSlotKeys rest

-- `moduleMarkCtx ms mid prog`: core (`mid == ""`) is marked with the unsplit set and
-- the core-scoped shadow map (#2153).  A user module gets the split set, scoped by the
-- filter below.
--
-- CORE'S rp/arg SETS ARE S1-FILTERED TOO, and the argument that they need not be is
-- retired.  It read: "core's references to its own standalones are all mangled
-- `core__<n>` by the time this runs, so neither set can match one."  #2809 moved
-- mangling AFTER elaboration, so core's references now carry the names its author
-- wrote and a USER interface method spelled like a core standalone matches them.
-- MEASURED on `test/prelude_shadow_census.ledger`'s own probe shape — `interface Ifc c
-- where identity : c -> Int` beside `impl Ifc Int`, in a module that defines no
-- `identity` — `check` and `run` accept and print 1 while `build` died `E-PANIC: no
-- impl of method 'identity' for type 'List'`: core's own `identity` call, on a `List`,
-- had been rewritten to a dispatch on the USER's interface.  Four ledger rows
-- (`identity`, `otherwise`, `arbitraryList`, `arbitraryString`) moved PASS -> FAIL_BUILD
-- that way.  The rule applied is the one `coreShadowMapFor` already applies to the
-- shadow map for the same reason: an interface declared in a USER module is not
-- nameable in `core`, so no `core.mdk` occurrence is one of its method occurrences.
-- Same fail-OPEN guard as `nameableIfaceShadows`: an absent graph index leaves the sets
-- unfiltered rather than emptying them.
moduleMarkCtx : GraphCtx ->
  MarkSets ->
  String ->
  List Decl ->
  OrdMap Scheme ->
  MarkCtx
moduleMarkCtx gctx ms mid prog imported =
  let candidates = methodMarkCtx gctx ms mid prog
  let local = namesToSet (declTopFnNames prog) omEmpty
  -- A module's own extern denotes itself wherever the module spells it, as its
  -- own function named like an interface method does (SHADOW-SEMANTICS S2's
  -- definer arm), so its occurrences are never method occurrences.
  let externs = namesToSet (declExternNames prog) omEmpty
  MarkCtx {
    mcRp = IdMap.difference candidates.mcRp externs,
    mcAn = IdMap.difference candidates.mcAn externs,
    mcSm =
      filterList
        (entry => omHasKey (fst entry) local || omHasKey (snd entry) imported)
        candidates.mcSm,
  }

-- ⚠️ THE IMPLICIT-PRELUDE ARM ABOVE IS LOAD-BEARING, AND ITS ABSENCE WAS MEASURED.
-- The prelude is in scope in EVERY module under BARE names and contributes NO `DUse`
-- decl, so a walk over the module's imports cannot see it: a
-- prelude standalone shadowed by a USER interface method (S1-PRELUDE (a), the
-- `x4_prelude_standalone_live_impl_receiver` / `x5_prelude_constrained_standalone_live_impl`
-- cells) mangles to `core__isEven` with no import form naming `isEven`, so without this
-- arm the entry was dropped and both cells went `DIFF`/FAIL — the prelude standalone's
-- `False` where the ruling requires the interface method's `True`. The prelude is also
-- the one module that CANNOT be alias-imported (`import core as C` → `Unbound variable:
-- C.eq`, SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md §1.1's table), so bare is its only spelling and this arm
-- admits nothing the alias case could have written differently.

-- typecheck one module (seeded like checkModuleFull) AND immediately stamp the
-- EMethodAt route refs it just recorded.  `recordModuleStart` marks the goal channel
-- before inference, so on return the module's window holds exactly THIS module's
-- sites; the tyvar cells are still bound (the next module's `freshModuleCtx` hasn't run
-- yet), so resolveSites reads each site's resolved result type.
-- E4: ALSO stamp this module's ARG-position sites
-- (the `GKArgStamp` goals in the same window) from their now-
-- resolved discriminating-argument monos — the multi-module analogue of
-- the shared `resolveArgStamps`. [implDecls] is core + every earlier module +
-- this module, so a cross-module parametric `requires` element dict resolves; a
-- still-unresolvable case stays RNone (arg-tag fallback).  activeDictVars (the
-- constraint-var → dict-param map registerConstraintRegs built in checkModuleFull)
-- is also still bound, so a tyvar receiver routes RDict.
elabModuleStamp : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List (String, Scheme) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl ->
  (ModuleBindings, List Decl, ModuleCtx)
-- multi-line RHS: the indented `:=` form is legal but not seed-parseable yet (#1744)
-- lint-disable-next-line rule-prefer-assign-op
elabModuleStamp prev mid seedVars accData implDecls prog =
  -- Stampers execute after graph inference via `drainStampQueue`, not here.
  -- See `StampCtx` and `moduleStampOrder` for the replay mechanism.
  checkModuleFullImpl
    prev.mcGraph
    (checkRunResidue prev)
    mid
    (plainModuleSeed seedVars)
    accData
    implDecls
    prog

-- USER modules do NOT come through `elabModuleStamp`: `graphModuleWorker` runs
-- `checkModuleFullDiags` for them on both selections, so a user module's
-- constructor/match ORACLE is seeded from its own decls and `runFinalChecks`
-- (coherence, interface cycles, phantom methods, super impls) runs, identically for
-- `check` and for `build`.  The CORE pass stays here: neither selection runs
-- `checkModuleFullDiags` over the prelude, so seeding an oracle from core or running
-- coherence over it would be a new population, not a shared one.
-- DRIVER-COLLAPSE Phase 2: pass the return-position method names (was `[]`) so
-- resolveSite's RDict-case routes a RETURN-position method site RDictFwd (forward the
-- enclosing dict's nested reqs) rather than RDict (arg-position). The former path
-- passes `returnPosMethodNames prog2`; the empty list mis-stamped a parametric-impl
-- body's inner return-position method (`impl Default (List a) requires Default a where
-- def = [def]` — the inner `def` must be RDictFwd:$dict_def_0, not RDict) → eval
-- `no matching impl for dispatch` (nested_instance_dicts).  `implDecls` is this
-- module's full impl universe (core/earlier-modules ++ prog), the analogue of flat's
-- whole-program `prog2`.

-- Phase 151 / Gap G: stamp this module's comparison-operator binop sites.
-- ungated (preserving the former path's call to `resolveBinopSites`
-- unconditionally) so the EVAL path also dispatches `==`/`<`/… to user/derived
-- Eq/Ord impls (adt_deriving_ord / record_deriving_ord).  No-op when
-- pendingBinopSites is empty (no comparison-operator site) → golden type-only
-- path leaves them RNone → dictPass-skipped → byte-identical.  Gap #21: binop route
-- stamping emits `RKey key []` (empty element reqs), which only narrows the method
-- VMulti and applies ZERO dicts,
-- so even a RECURSIVE user Eq impl (json's `impl Eq Json`) dispatches inner
-- operands by arg-tag without over-applying — no suppression needed.

-- C5: LAST among the route-stampers (after resolveSites AND resolveArgStamps) so the
-- receiver-grounded RLocal/RNone overrides whatever those stamped on the SAME ref —
-- resolveSites mis-stamps RKey<resultType> (eval path) and resolveArgStamps stamps
-- RKey<receiverHead> (emit path), both wrong for a standalone-shadow site.

-- E6: fill THIS module's `=>`-constrained-fn EDictAt routes (the call sites
-- prePassDictArg marked) so the emitter supplies the matching dict ARGUMENT —
-- realizeRecDictApps for self/mutually-recursive calls, resolveDictApps for the
-- normal ones.  ARGSTAMP-UNIFY Phase 4: unconditional on BOTH paths — the eval path
-- also marks the RETURN-position constrained fns (sum/product/when/unless) EDictAt
-- via moduleDictNames, so their call-site routes must resolve here too.  No-op when
-- nothing was marked (pendingDictApps/pendingRecDictApps empty → golden drivers
-- byte-identical).

-- G7: fill each foldMap-style method occurrence's methRoutes from the monos its
-- `Monoid m` constraint resolved to at the call site (List vs String), so the
-- default's entry receives the right per-call method dictionary.
-- Independent of the body-side dict routing (the emitter restamps the body's
-- cross-interface `empty` to its `$dict_<method>_<slot>` param directly).
-- ARGSTAMP-UNIFY Phase 4: run unconditionally on every path (single elaboration
-- mode), preserving the former path (which
-- calls resolveMethodDicts unconditionally) — a method with its OWN method-level
-- constraint (`build : Num e => e -> t`) needs its method-dict route filled so its
-- impl clause binds the leading dict param instead of mis-binding it into the first
-- value param (method_constraint_impl_offset: was `non-exhaustive match`).  No-op
-- when pendingMethodDicts is empty → golden drivers byte-identical.

-- THE stamper order, run once per module by `drainStampQueue`.
moduleStampOrder : List StampStep
moduleStampOrder = [
  SSNumlitFloats,
  SSReturnSites,
  SSBinopSites,
  SSUnopSites,
  SSArithSites,
  SSArgStamps,
  SSRLocalSites,
  SSRecDictApps,
  SSDictApps,
  SSMethodDicts,
]

-- Whether a finding at [loc] is live: it is located, at one of [live]'s spans.
export
isLiveSpan : OrdMap Unit -> Option Loc -> Bool
isLiveSpan _ None = False
isLiveSpan live loc = omHasKey (locKey loc) live

-- [stamp] is the record the drain entered for [ctx].
runStampSteps : ModuleCtx -> StampCtx -> List StampStep -> Unit
runStampSteps stamp ctx steps = each (runStampStep stamp ctx) steps

-- the numeric-literal channel's window, the counterpart of `goalsSince`
numlitSince : GraphCtx -> Int -> List (Mono, Ref (Option Float), Int, Ref Route)
numlitSince gctx mark =
  moduleWindow gctx.graphRun.numlitN.value mark gctx.graphRun.numlitRefs.value

-- The stamp context of the module [mid] whose record is [mctx]: the module's run
-- fields, and its tables dropped (`moduleCtxFrom`).
stampCtxOf : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List Decl ->
  List Obligation ->
  List (Mono, Ref (Option Float), Int, Ref Route) ->
  StampCtx
stampCtxOf mctx mid implDecls goals numlits =
  let dropped = blankModuleCtx mctx.mcGraph mid
  dropped.mcCells.superDeclsRef := filterList isInterfaceDecl implDecls
  StampCtx {
    scModule = mid,
    scModuleCtx = moduleCtxFrom False mctx dropped dropped dropped,
    scRpNames = returnPosMethodNames implDecls,
    scGoals = goals,
    scNumlits = numlits,
    scLiveLocs = liveLocsOf mctx goals,
  }

-- The spans of [goals] and of the module's admitted-set occurrences whose types
-- mention a variable of a live root (`GraphRun.liveRoots`): their evidence and
-- verdicts rest on what quiescence leaves that variable.
liveLocsOf : ModuleCtx -> List Obligation -> List String
liveLocsOf mctx goals =
  let ids = flatMap monoUnboundIds mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.liveRoots.value
  if isEmptyL ids then
    []
  else
    let live = fold (acc i => IdMap.set i () acc) Tip ids
    let mentions =
      ms => anyList (m => anyList (i => IdMap.has i live) (monoUnboundIds m)) ms
    spanKeys
      (map (o => o.oLoc) (filterList (o => mentions (goalMonos o)) goals)
        ++ filterMap
          ((_, m, loc) => if mentions [m] then Some loc else None)
          mctx.mcCells.admittedOccObls.value)

-- The span keys (`locKey`) of the located [locs].  An unlocated goal or occurrence
-- names no span, so no unlocated finding is joined to it (`isLiveSpan`).
export
spanKeys : List (Option Loc) -> List String
spanKeys [] = []
spanKeys (None :: rest) = spanKeys rest
spanKeys (loc :: rest) = locKey loc :: spanKeys rest

isInterfaceDecl : Decl -> Bool
isInterfaceDecl (DAttrib _ d) = isInterfaceDecl d
isInterfaceDecl (DInterface {  }) = True
isInterfaceDecl _ = False

-- This module's windows, cut now — see `goalsOfKindIn`.  [mctx] is the record the
-- module was checked in.
enqueueStampCtx : ModuleCtx -> String -> List Decl -> Unit
enqueueStampCtx mctx mid implDecls =
  let mk = currentModuleMarks mctx.mcGraph ()
  let ctx =
    stampCtxOf
      mctx
      mid
      implDecls
      (goalsSince mctx.mcGraph mk.mGoals)
      (numlitSince mctx.mcGraph mk.mNumlit)
  mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.stampCtxs :=
    ctx :: mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.stampCtxs.value

stampNoting : ModuleCtx -> (SiteCtx -> Obligation -> Unit) -> Obligation -> Unit
stampNoting stamp resolve o =
  let acc = Ref innerNone
  resolve { siteFor stamp | sxInner = Some acc } o
  o.oInner := innerOr o.oInner.value acc.value

runStampStep : ModuleCtx -> StampCtx -> StampStep -> Unit
runStampStep mctx ctx SSNumlitFloats = setNumlitFloatsGo ctx.scNumlits
runStampStep stamp ctx SSReturnSites =
  let rpNames = omFromNames ctx.scRpNames omEmpty
  stampEach
    stamp
    (sx o => resolveSites sx rpNames (siteEntry o))
    GKReturnSite
    ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSBinopSites =
  stampEach stamp (sx o => resolveOpSites sx True (siteEntry o)) GKBinopSite ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSUnopSites =
  stampEach stamp (sx o => resolveOpSites sx False (siteEntry o)) GKUnopSite ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSArithSites =
  stampEach stamp (_ o => resolveArithSites (arithEntry o)) GKArithSite ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSArgStamps =
  stampEach stamp (sx o => resolveArgStamps sx (siteEntry o)) GKArgStamp ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSRLocalSites =
  stampEach stamp (sx o => resolveRLocalSites sx (siteEntry o)) GKRLocalSite ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSRecDictApps =
  stampEach
    stamp
    (sx o => realizeRecDictApps sx (recDictAppEntry o))
    GKRecDictApp
    ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSDictApps =
  stampEach stamp (sx o => resolveDictApps sx (dictAppEntry o)) GKDictApp ctx
runStampStep stamp ctx SSMethodDicts =
  stampEach
    stamp
    (sx o => resolveMethodDicts sx (methodDictEntry o))
    GKMethodDict
    ctx

-- Stamps [ctx]'s goals of kind [k] one at a time, in channel order, and ORs what
-- each stamp noted below its destination's top level into that goal's `oInner`.
stampEach : ModuleCtx ->
  (SiteCtx -> Obligation -> Unit) ->
  GoalKind ->
  StampCtx ->
  Unit
stampEach stamp resolve k ctx =
  fold (_ o => stampNoting stamp resolve o) () (goalsOfKindIn k ctx.scGoals)

-- #2548 (ARCH M3/Q2, DICT §6.2 T4): ONE ordered resolve pass over the whole graph,
-- at quiescence.  Every module's goals are stamped after every module has been
-- inferred, so a goal in an early module is decided against the final solution
-- rather than against the solution as it stood when that module closed.
--
-- The per-module context is REPLAYED, not re-derived (see `StampCtx`), and restored
-- afterwards so `dictPassModulesIfEnabled` — which runs next — sees the state the
-- last module left, exactly as it does today.
-- #2705: the drain at the core pass's freeze (`checkCoreMemoized`), at a recording
-- module's end and at a keyed drive's graph end (`diagsServe`).  Nothing is
-- published: a check driver has no reader of the evidence table.
--
-- The sticky type-error cells are saved before the drain and restored after it, so
-- a recorded interface never carries a drain's diagnostics.  An unkeyed drive
-- (`driveGraphK`) keeps them instead; the two agree because the drain raises none on
-- an accepted program.  The drain's evidence holes are returned, not recorded: a
-- per-module diagnostics list is closed before any drain, so the caller attaches
-- them to it (`attachEvidenceHoles`).
checkGraphFinish : ModuleCtx -> List DrainFinding
checkGraphFinish mctx =
  let savedSticky = mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsSticky.value
  let savedStickyDiags = mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsStickyDiags.value
  let holes = drainStampQueue mctx
  mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsSticky := savedSticky
  mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsStickyDiags := savedStickyDiags
  holes

verdictFinding : String -> Bool -> TcDiag -> DrainFinding
verdictFinding mid live d = DrainFinding {
  dfModule = mid,
  dfDiag = d,
  dfVerdict = True,
  dfLive = live,
}

-- What [act] records in the type-error channel of [mctx], the current record, taken
-- back out of it and out of the sticky one: a drain runs after every module's
-- diagnostics list closed, so its caller attaches them (`attachDrainFindings`).  The
-- dedup state [act] reads and writes stays, so a verdict the module already reported is
-- not repeated.
captureTypeErrors : ModuleCtx -> (Unit -> Unit) -> List TcDiag
captureTypeErrors mctx act =
  let w = mctx.mcCells.typeErrors
  let items = w.items.value
  let mark = wMark w
  let sticky = mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsSticky.value
  let stickyDiags = mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsStickyDiags.value
  act ()
  let added = wWindow w mark
  w.items := items
  w.n := mark
  mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsSticky := sticky
  mctx.mcGraph.typeErrorsStickyDiags := stickyDiags
  reverseL added

-- Runs every queued stamping context, then judges the evidence they finished.
-- Returns the verdicts the drain decides (held live-root goals, admitted-set
-- occurrences) and one `T-UNROUTED-DISPATCH` per hole, each under its module.
-- [saved] is the record the drain begins with; each stamp context's walk runs in the
-- record the drain enters for it (`enterStampCtx`).
drainStampQueue : ModuleCtx -> List DrainFinding
drainStampQueue saved =
  let ctxs = reverseL saved.mcGraph.graphRun.stampCtxs.value
  defaultLiveNumRoots saved
  let held = judgeLiveGoals saved ctxs
  let verdicts = runStampCtxs saved ctxs
  let liveLocs = omFromNames (flatMap (c => c.scLiveLocs) ctxs) omEmpty
  let holes =
    map
      ((mid, d) => DrainFinding {
        dfModule = mid,
        dfDiag = d,
        dfVerdict = False,
        dfLive = isLiveSpan liveLocs (tcLoc d),
      })
      (judgeEvidence saved.mcGraph ctxs)
  materializeBinderTypes saved.mcGraph ()
  saved.mcGraph.graphRun.stampCtxs := []
  held ++ verdicts ++ holes

-- The completeness judgment (`types/evidence_complete.mdk`) over the evidence this
-- drain finished: every method cell minted since the last drain, and the goals of
-- [ctxs] whose destination is not a method cell.  A return-site, arg-stamp or
-- RLocal goal writes its cell's dispatch route and a method-dict goal its method
-- dictionaries, so those are judged once, as the cell.
judgeEvidence : GraphCtx -> List StampCtx -> List (String, TcDiag)
judgeEvidence gctx ctxs =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  let lo = g.evJudged.value
  g.evJudged := g.evCounter.value
  let base = g.evBase
  let cellHoles =
    flatMap
      ((a, b) => judgeCells g.evCells.value (a - base) (b - base) [])
      (unjudgedRanges lo g.evCounter.value g.evScopedJudged.value)
  let goalHoles = flatMap (c => flatMap (judgeGoal c.scModule) c.scGoals) ctxs
  dedupBy holeKey (cellHoles ++ goalHoles)

holeKey : (String, TcDiag) -> String
holeKey (m, TcDiag _ _ loc msg _ _) =
  "\{lenKey m}\{lenKey (locGoalKey loc)}\{msg}"

-- The cells in slots [i, hi) (ordinals less `evBase`), last first onto [acc].  A
-- cell no inference reached (no arity) carries no answer to judge.
judgeCells : Array (Option EvCell) ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  List (String, TcDiag) ->
  List (String, TcDiag)
judgeCells arr i hi acc
  | i >= hi || i >= arrayLength arr = acc
  | otherwise = match arrayGetUnsafe i arr
    Some c => match c.ecArity.value
      Some _ =>
        let row =
          OccurrenceRow
            c.ecName.value
            c.ecIface.value
            c.ecTag.value
            c.ecImpl.value
            c.ecMeth.value
        judgeCells
          arr
          (i + 1)
          hi
          (holeDiags (evIdModule c.ecId) c.ecLoc.value c.ecInner.value row
            ++ acc)
      None => judgeCells arr (i + 1) hi acc
    None => judgeCells arr (i + 1) hi acc

judgeGoal : String -> Obligation -> List (String, TcDiag)
judgeGoal mid o = match (o.oPayload, evValueOf o.oDest)
  (GPDictApp app, EvMany rs) =>
    holeDiags
      mid
      o.oLoc
      o.oInner.value
      (DictAppRow app.pdaCallee (map (r => r.irName) app.pdaIfaces) rs)
  (GPRecDictApp (RecDictApp _ callee _ _ _ _), EvMany rs) =>
    holeDiags mid o.oLoc o.oInner.value (DictAppRow callee [] rs)
  (GPArith _, EvOne r) => holeDiags mid o.oLoc o.oInner.value (SiteRow r)
  (GPSite _ _ _, EvOne r) =>
    if goalKindTag o.oKind == goalKindTag GKBinopSite
      || goalKindTag o.oKind == goalKindTag GKUnopSite then
      holeDiags mid o.oLoc o.oInner.value (SiteRow r)
    else
      []
  _ => []

holeDiags : String ->
  Option Loc ->
  Inner ->
  EvidenceRow ->
  List (String, TcDiag)
holeDiags mid loc inner row = match rowHoleWith inner row
  None => []
  Some (_, msg) => [(mid, TcDiag "T-UNROUTED-DISPATCH" 1 loc msg None None)]

-- Each drain verdict joins the errors of the module it belongs to, and each hole
-- does unless that module then has errors: a hole beside a type error is usually its
-- consequence.  A live finding is dropped when any module of [perMod] has errors,
-- since the live root it rests on may be one an erroneous importer grounded or left
-- open.  A finding in no module of [perMod] is a module the drive has no list for,
-- which only the prelude is.
attachDrainFindings : List DrainFinding -> List ModDiags -> List ModDiags
attachDrainFindings [] perMod = perMod
attachDrainFindings findings perMod =
  let orphans =
    filterList (f => not (anyList (pm => fst pm == f.dfModule) perMod)) findings
  match orphans
    [] => ()
    f :: _ =>
      panic
        "evidence hole in module `\{f.dfModule}`, which has no diagnostics list: \{tcMsg f.dfDiag}"
  let erred = anyList (pm => isNonEmptyL (modDiagErrs pm)) perMod
  let kept = if erred then filterList (f => not f.dfLive) findings else findings
  map (pm => findingsOnto kept pm) perMod

modDiagErrs : ModDiags -> List TcDiag
modDiagErrs (_, (_, errs, _)) = errs

findingsOnto : List DrainFinding -> ModDiags -> ModDiags
findingsOnto findings (mid, (schemes, errs, warns)) =
  let mine = filterList (f => f.dfModule == mid) findings
  let verdicts = map (f => f.dfDiag) (filterList (f => f.dfVerdict) mine)
  match errs ++ verdicts
    [] => (mid, (schemes, map (f => f.dfDiag) mine, warns))
    all => (mid, (schemes, all, warns))

-- Read every queued binder's type cell into the graph's runtime-type table, now
-- that the stampers have run and nothing left in the graph can refine a drained
-- module's types.  Runs at every drain, including the one before a memo snapshot,
-- so a snapshot carries only materialized rows.
materializeBinderTypes : GraphCtx -> Unit -> Unit
materializeBinderTypes gctx _ =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  match g.binderPending.value
    [] => ()
    pending =>
      let cells = cellTypeHeads gctx.declEnvsRef.value.deAllDecls
      let isCell = n o => omHasKey (cellHeadKey n o) cells
      g.binderRows :=
        fold
          (acc p => addBinderRow (materializeBinder isCell p) acc)
          g.binderRows.value
          (reverseL pending)
      g.binderPending := []

materializeBinder : (String -> TyConOrigin -> Bool) ->
  PendingBinder ->
  BinderRow
materializeBinder isCell (PendingBinder bid name t arity signed) = BinderRow {
  brId = bid,
  brName = name,
  brType = runtimeTypeOf isCell t,
  -- A solved type with fewer arrows than the declared parameters fixes nothing.
  brReturns =
    map
      (n =>
        optionOr RTValue (map (runtimeTypeOf isCell) (resultAfterArrows n t)))
      arity,
  brSigned = signed,
}

-- The type heads whose values are constructor cells: every `data` and `newtype`
-- declaration in the graph except an `extern data` one, keyed by identity.
cellTypeHeads : List Decl -> OrdMap Unit
cellTypeHeads decls = fold (acc d => addCellHead d acc) omEmpty decls

addCellHead : Decl -> OrdMap Unit -> OrdMap Unit
addCellHead (DData { dataName = n, dataOrigin = o, dataExtern = ext, ... }) acc =
  if ext then acc else omInsert (cellHeadKey n o) () acc
addCellHead (DNewtype { newtypeName = n, newtypeOrigin = o, ... }) acc =
  omInsert (cellHeadKey n o) () acc
addCellHead (DAttrib _ d) acc = addCellHead d acc
addCellHead _ acc = acc

cellHeadKey : String -> TyConOrigin -> String
cellHeadKey n OriginBuiltin = "builtin|\{n}"
cellHeadKey n OriginUnresolved = "unresolved|\{n}"
cellHeadKey n (OriginModule m) = "module \{m}|\{n}"

-- Stamps each context in turn and decides its admitted-set occurrences
-- (`checkAdmittedOccObls`), with the selector their routes commit through, against
-- the same final solution.
runStampCtxs : ModuleCtx -> List StampCtx -> List DrainFinding
runStampCtxs saved ctxs =
  reverseL (fold (acc ctx => reverseL (runStampCtx saved ctx) ++ acc) [] ctxs)

runStampCtx : ModuleCtx -> StampCtx -> List DrainFinding
runStampCtx saved ctx =
  let stamp = enterStampCtx saved ctx
  refileDeterminedRows stamp ()
  runStampSteps stamp ctx moduleStampOrder
  recordEvidence saved.mcGraph ctx.scGoals
  let liveSpans = omFromNames ctx.scLiveLocs omEmpty
  map
    (d => verdictFinding ctx.scModule (isLiveSpan liveSpans (tcLoc d)) d)
    (captureTypeErrors stamp (_ => checkAdmittedOccObls stamp ()))

-- #2549 M2: publish this module's solved evidence, AFTER its stampers have run and
-- READ BACK OUT OF THE CELLS THEY WROTE.  Deriving the table any other way would make
-- it a second answer that can disagree with the cells; derived this way it cannot.
recordEvidence : GraphCtx -> List Obligation -> Unit
recordEvidence gctx gs =
  let g = gctx.graphRun
  let _ = map (noteEvidenceObservation gctx) gs
  g.evTable := evEntriesOf gs ++ g.evTable.value

evEntriesOf : List Obligation -> EvTable
evEntriesOf gs = map (o => EvEntry o.oEv (evValueOf o.oDest)) gs

evValueOf : EvDest -> EvVal
evValueOf (EvRoute r) = EvOne !r
evValueOf (EvRoutes rs) = EvMany !rs

-- Writes `mangledShadowMapRef`, `argDispatchIdxByIdRef` and `markSetsRef` as a side
-- effect: the first two are read by the inference of a marked tree (P0-18 shadow
-- recovery, `argDispatchOf`), the third by `checkBodyImpl`, which marks each module's
-- groups on the schedule — so the driver that marks must be the driver that sets
-- them.  Empty / index-only on the un-mangled check path, exactly as the emit path
-- derives them.  `markSetsOf` below is the function; unkeyed, its prelude half is
-- `preludeMarkFactsOf coreDecls`.

preludeMarkFactsOf : List Decl -> PreludeMarkFacts
preludeMarkFactsOf coreDecls = PreludeMarkFacts {
  pmfReturnPos = returnPosMethodNames coreDecls,
  pmfMethodConstraints = methodConstraintNames coreDecls,
  pmfArgDispatch = argDispatchIndices coreDecls,
  pmfArgDispatchById = argDispatchIndicesById coreDecls,
  pmfConstrainedNames = constrainedSigNames coreDecls,
}

-- Install the module's marking state at module start.  Reads the graph's mark sets
-- off the driver preamble; a Module arm reached without one is a driver bug, and
-- fails loud rather than marking nothing.
beginModuleMarking : ModuleCtx ->
  String ->
  List Decl ->
  OrdMap Int ->
  ModuleSeed ->
  Unit
beginModuleMarking mctx mid prog top seed =
  let ms = match mctx.mcGraph.markSetsRef.value
    Some s => s
    None =>
      panic
        "checkBodyImpl: Module arm entered with no mark sets (no driver preamble ran)"
  -- Core imports nothing, so the dict names nameable in it are its own `=>`
  -- signatures, the set its `dictPass` gives parameters to.  A user definition that
  -- shares a bare name with a core one is a different definition.
  let known = match mid
    "" => constrainedSigNames prog
    _ => dedup (ms.msBareDictNames ++ mctx.mcGraph.promotionHarvestRef.value)
  let aliases = aliasDictNames mctx.mcGraph known ms.msUnits [(mid, prog)]
  mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs.lasNext := (mid, 0)
  mctx.mcGraph.graphRun.localAbs.lasMinted := []
  mctx.mcCells.markingRef := Some ModuleMarking {
    mmCtx = moduleMarkCtx mctx.mcGraph ms mid prog seed.msImportedValues,
    mmTop = top,
    mmDictSet = Ref (omFromNames (known ++ aliases) omEmpty),
    mmUserNames = omFromNames (declTopFnNames prog) seed.msImportedNames,
    mmExterns = omFromNames (declExternNames prog) seed.msImportedExterns,
  }

-- The stamped twin of the group's marked clauses — what inference reads.  Binding
-- ids are minted over the module's declaration heads (`stampTopScope`), so stamping
-- one group at a time yields the ids `stampBindingIds` would have.
stampGroupClauses : ModuleMarking ->
  List String ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr))
stampGroupClauses mm members grouped =
  mapGroupClauses (stampClauseWith mm.mmTop) members grouped

-- The module's marked tree: its binding groups' marked clauses written back into the
-- declarations in source order, then the remaining bodies (impl, default, prop,
-- test) marked with the module's final dict-name set — they are inferred
-- after every group, so every promotion the module made is in the set by then.
finishModuleMarking : ModuleMarking ->
  TcEnv ->
  OrdMap (List (List Pat, Expr)) ->
  List Decl ->
  List Decl
finishModuleMarking mm env grouped prog =
  markTailDecls
    env.teDyn.dcModule
    mm.mmCtx
    mm.mmDictSet.value
    (grantNameIn env)
    (rebuildGroupDecls grouped prog)

-- The stamped twin of the tail declarations, for their inference; binding groups
-- were stamped as the schedule reached them and are not walked again.
stampTailDecls : OrdMap Int -> List Decl -> List Decl
stampTailDecls top decls = map (stampTailDecl top) decls

stampTailDecl : OrdMap Int -> Decl -> Decl
stampTailDecl _ (d@(DFunDef _ _ _ _ _ _)) = d
stampTailDecl _ (d@(DLetGroup _ _)) = d
stampTailDecl top (DAttrib attrs d) = DAttrib attrs (stampTailDecl top d)
stampTailDecl top d = stampDeclWith top d

schemeLines : List (String, PubScheme) -> List String
schemeLines [] = []
schemeLines ((n, p) :: rest) = "\{n} : \{ppPubScheme p}" :: schemeLines rest
